From scattered records to a connected model

This running demo reads three JSON files and answers queries in C++. HTML displays the results.

01 · PRESERVE

Keep the original evidence

Each source has a URL, capture date, and original field values. Adafruit’s Pico 2 description says both 512KB and 520KB.

data/raw_records.json → R05
02 · ORGANIZE

Give each thing an identity

A retailer listing and a board design get different IDs. Each listing keeps its own prices and availability.

L_ADA_6006 → V_PICO2
03 · CONNECT

Link the evidence

Both Pico 2 listings connect to a shared design. That design connects to RP2350 and a manufacturer datasheet.

data/relationships.json
04 · QUERY

Answer with a traceable result

C++ groups accepted listing mappings by product and retailer. It finds two shared designs and leaves Teensy as a candidate.

cpp/server.cpp → summary()Open the actual API response ↗

WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU SELECT PICO 2

The browser asks. C++ follows the IDs.

JavaScript sends an HTTP request. The C++ inspect() function collects related listings, claims, source records, and unresolved issues. The browser renders that JSON.

// dist/app.js
const detail = await api(
  '/api/entity?id=V_PICO2'
);

// C++ HTTP route calls:
model.inspect("V_PICO2");
What works today

Local search, linked records, evidence inspection, a relationship graph, and repeatable model queries. Source collection and normalization in this pilot were prepared manually. Automatic database connections, continuous refresh, data uploads, and AI-agent integration are future work.
